Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.
Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.
The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.
“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.
For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”
He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”
He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”
But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”
When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast , Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”
He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”
In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

Komisyonda kabul edilen enerjiye ve sosyal güvenliğe ilişkin düzenlemeleri de içeren kanun teklifiyle, Anayasa Mahkemesinin iptal kararı doğrultusunda, Jandarma Teşkilat, Görev ve Yetkileri Kanunu'nda değişikliğe gidiliyor. Böylece Jandarma Genel Komutanlığı ve Sahil Güvenlik Komutanlığında istihdam edilecek muvazzaf subay ve astsubay adayları ile fakülte ve meslek yüksekokuluna alınacak adaylarda aranacak niteliklerin ve başvuran adaylara uygulanacak sınavların usul ve esaslarına ilişkin temel ilke ve çerçeve belirleniyor.
Mesleki Eğitim Kanunu'nda yapılan değişiklikle, aday çırak, çırak, işletmelerde mesleki eğitim gören, staj veya tamamlayıcı eğitime devam eden öğrencilere verilen ücretlere sağlanan devlet katkısında Cumhurbaşkanına tanınan uzatma yetkisinin süresi her defasında bir eğitim ve öğretim yılı olmak üzere 15 eğitim ve öğretim yılına çıkarılacak. Devlet desteğinin uygulanmasına ilişkin usul ve esasları belirlemeye Cumhurbaşkanı yetkili olacak. Düzenleme, 14 Eylül 2026'dan itibaren geçerli olmak üzere yayımı tarihinde yürürlüğe girecek.
İşsizlik Sigortası Kanunu'nda yapılan değişiklikle, ilave istihdamın sağlanması ve özel politika gerektiren kadın, genç ve mesleki ve teknik eğitime ilişkin belge sahibi olan işsizlerin istihdamının desteklenmesi için verilen teşvik 31 Aralık 2028'e kadar devam ettirilecek ve uygulamanın 31 Aralık 2029'a kadar uzatılabilmesi için Cumhurbaşkanına yetki verilecek.
Anayasa Mahkemesinin iptal kararı doğrultusunda, Doğal Gaz Piyasası Kanunu'nda değişikliğe gidiliyor. Yüzen LNG terminallerinin belirli bir süre ve kapsam dahilinde yerlerinden ayrılarak başka bölgelerde hizmet vermelerine Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı görüşü alınarak Enerji Piyasası Düzenleme Kurulu tarafından izin verilebilecek.
BOTAŞ'ın 31 Aralık 2026 ile 31 Aralık 2027 arasında Ticaret Bakanlığına bağlı tahsil dairelerine ödemesi gereken her türlü vergi, fon ve paylar, BOTAŞ'ın Hazineden oluşmuş ve/veya 31 Aralık 2027 tarihi sonuna kadar oluşacak görevlendirme alacaklarına karşılık, merkezi yönetim bütçesinin gelir ve gider hesaplarıyla ilişkilendirilmeksizin mahsup suretiyle Ticaret Bakanlığınca aylık olarak terkin edilecek ve terkin edilecek her türlü vergi asıllarına ilişkin feri alacak hesaplanmayacak.
Bu düzenleme kapsamında yapılacak mahsup işlemine konu görevlendirme bedeli hesaplamasında BOTAŞ'ın muhasebe kayıt ve belgeleri esas alınacak. Kamu İktisadi Teşebbüsleri Hakkında Kanun Hükmünde Kararname'de öngörülen usule uygun yapılan inceleme sonucunda hesaplanan görevlendirme bedeli, Ticaret Bakanlığı tarafından yapılan terkin tutarlarından az olduğunun tespit edilmesi halinde BOTAŞ tarafından yükümlülükler faizsiz yerine getirilecek ve söz konusu tutar Genel Bütçeye gelir kaydedilecek.
Bu hüküm kapsamında yapılacak mahsup ve terkin işlemleri, terkin kararı alınması nedeniyle mahsup edilecek tutarlar dışında kalan görevlendirme bedellerinin ödenmesine engel teşkil etmeyecek. İdarenin bu bedellere ilişkin ödeme yetkisini ortadan kaldırmayacak veya zamanını sınırlandırmayacak. Bu düzenleme kapsamında BOTAŞ'ın Hazineden görevlendirme bedeli alacağı tutarını tespit etmeye ve mahsup suretiyle yapılacak terkin işlemlerini belirlemeye Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı yetkili olacak.
Anayasa Mahkemesinin iptal kararı doğrultusunda Polis Yüksek Öğretim Kanunu'nda yapılan değişiklikle, polis meslek yüksekokullarına alınacak öğrencilerde aranacak şartların kanuni dayanağa kavuşturulması, eğitim ve öğretim hakkına ilişkin sınırlamaların kanunilik ilkesine uygun hale getirilmesi, hukuki belirlilik ve öngörülebilirliğin sağlanması ve idarenin düzenleme yetkisinin anayasal sınırlar içerisinde kullanılmasının temini amaçlanıyor.
Yenilenebilir Enerji Kaynaklarının Elektrik Enerjisi Üretimi Amaçlı Kullanımına İlişkin Kanun'da düzenlemeye gidiliyor. Buna göre, yenilenebilir enerji kaynak alanları ve bağlantı kapasitelerinin tahsisi yarışmayla yapılacak. Yarışmaya dair kapsam, teknik ve idari şartlar, diğer bilgiler ile yarışmada kapalı teklif, açık eksiltme veya açık artırma yöntemlerinden hangisinin ya da hangilerinin uygulanacağı yenilenebilir enerji kaynak alanlarının teknik ve idari özellikleri ile bağlantı kapasitesi de dikkate alınarak yarışma şartnamesinde belirtilecek.
10 yıllık süresini bitiren ve elektriksel kurulu gücü asgari 750 kilovat lisanssız üretim faaliyeti kapsamındaki tesisler için tesis sahibi tarafından talep edilmesi durumunda, lisans süresi boyunca elektrik piyasasında oluşan saatlik piyasa takas fiyatının düzenlemenin ilgili hükmü kapsamında tesis tipi bazında uygulanan güncel YEK Destekleme Mekanizması fiyatından fazla olması halinde aradaki fiyat farkının ve lisans alma bedelinin YEK Destekleme Mekanizmasına katkı bedeli şeklinde ödenmesi koşullarıyla lisanslı üretim faaliyetine geçilebilecek. Bu kapsamdaki başvurular için Enerji Piyasası Düzenleme Kurumu (EPDK) tarafından belirlenen kaynak bazında güncel birim yatırım tutarının yüzde 30'unu aşmayacak şekilde megavat başına uygulanacak lisans alma bedeli, lisans süresi ve lisanslı üretim faaliyetine geçilmesine ilişkin diğer hususlar EPDK tarafından belirlenecek.
Teklifle Sosyal Sigortalar ve Genel Sağlık Sigortası Kanunu'na geçici hükümler ekleniyor. Buna göre, 2026 yılında götürü bedel üzerinden hizmet alım sözleşmesi yapılmış kamu üniversitesi sağlık hizmeti sunucularının Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumuna (SGK) 31 Aralık 2026'ya kadar bu sözleşme kapsamında verdikleri tedavi hizmetlerine ilişkin toplam tahakkuk tutarının götürü bedel sözleşme tutarından düşük olması durumunda, aradaki fark terkin edilecek. Terkin edilen tutar, Bakanlık bütçesine bu amaçla tahsis edilecek ödenekten karşılanacak. Bu hükme ilişkin usul ve esaslar Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığının görüşü alınarak SGK tarafından belirlenecek.
Düzenlemeye göre, 1 Ocak 2017'den önceye ait olup, ödenmemiş genel sağlık sigortası primleri ile gecikme cezası ve gecikme zammı gibi feri alacaklarının tamamının tahsilinden vazgeçilecek. Bu hükmün yayımlandığı tarihe kadar söz konusu süreler için ödenmiş primler iade ve mahsup edilmeyecek.
Teklifle, kurumlar vergisi indirimli oran uygulamasının dışında bırakılan elektrik enerjisi üretim faaliyetinde bulunan kurumlar AK Parti'li milletvekillerinin verdiği önergeyle indirimli oran kapsamına alındı.
Oybirliğiyle kabul edilen önergeye göre, üretim faaliyetiyle uğraşan kıymetli maden ve petrol rafinerileri ile tütün mamulleri ve alkollü içki üreticilerine tatbik edilecek kurumlar vergisi, indirimli oran uygulamasının dışında bırakılacak. Bu hüküm, 2027 yılı ve izleyen vergilendirme dönemlerinde elde edilen kazançlara, özel hesap dönemine tabi kurumların ise 2027 yılında başlayan özel hesap dönemi ve izleyen vergilendirme dönemlerinde elde edilen kazançlarına uygulanmak üzere yayımı tarihinden itibaren yürürlüğe girecek.
Elektrik Piyasası Kanunu'nda yapılan değişikliğe göre, rüzgar veya güneş enerjisine dayalı üretim lisansı sahipleri tarafından yapılan elektriksel kapasite artışlarında megavat başına alınacak bedeller, kaynak bazında Kurum tarafından belirlenen güncel birim yatırım tutarının yüzde 50'sini aşmayacak şekilde arz güvenliğinin temini ilkeleri çerçevesinde TEİAŞ tarafından belirlenecek. Belirlenen bedeller lisans tadilinden önce defaten TEİAŞ tarafından tahsil edilecek. Tahsil edilen bedeller TEİAŞ'a gelir kaydedilecek.
Tasfiyesine Karar Verilen Bazı Yatırım Fonları Hakkında Kanun'un "Dışarıdan hizmet alımı ve uygulanacak hükümler" başlıklı hükmünde düzenleme yapılıyor. Buna göre, Kanun ile ilgili iş ve işlemlerde görevlendirilenler ile bu süreçlerle bağlantılı tasfiye veya devretme ve devralma işlemlerini yürüten mevduat bankaları ve katılım bankaları ile kalkınma ve yatırım bankaları ile bunların söz konusu eylem ve işlemleri yürütmekle görevlendirdikleri kişilerin, konusu suç teşkil eden fiilleri hariç olmak kaydıyla, görevleriyle ilgili 17 Eylül 2026'dan itibaren aldıkları kararlar ve yaptıkları eylem ve işlemler nedeniyle hukuki, idari ve mali sorumlulukları doğmayacak. Football players say they are ‘traumatized’ after being handcuffed and detained by police while waiting for rides home
Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them , prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun, in an incident that left them “fearing for their lives”.
The plaintiffs sued Omnilert, the company behind the AI gun-detection system, Baltimore county police, the board of education, individual officers and the school principal, alleging unlawful detention and search because of technological and human errors.
“These students were failed not only by a technology that is prone to false alerts, but also by the very adults meant to keep them safe when we send them to school,” said Damon Hewitt , the president and executive director of the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, which is representing the students. “Instead of this protection, they were met with guns and traumatized. And it could have been even worse.”
The incident took place last fall. The students had just wrapped up football practice on the evening of 20 October when their coach passed out bags of Doritos to the team, according to the complaint. Taki Allen, a junior at the time, took several bags and was with his friends near the picnic tables waiting for their ride, when six local police cruisers emerged with lights flashing. Many officers unholstered their weapons and the students put their hands in the air, the complaint said.
The legal complaint stated that the plaintiffs “were in shock and feared for their lives after being stopped, ordered to their knees, handcuffed and searched” by armed officers. One officer allegedly told them as he left the scene: “Hey, thanks for not running away, that would have been a real problem.”
The complaint described a chaotic series of events in which Omnilert’s AI gun-detection system flagged the chips bag as a firearm with 90% confidence. Omnilert Gun Detect system scans security footage for signs of firearms. “That alert kept going even after school staff and local police reviewed the image and determined it was a mistake,” the lawsuit stated.
While Omnilert markets its product as reliable and leading to “fewer false positives”, the lawsuit states that Maryland’s office of the inspector general for education “found that more than 99% of OGD Alerts in Baltimore County Public Schools were false positives that required no police response”.
Omnilert, the school principal, Baltimore police and the board of education did not immediately respond to a Guardian request for comment.
An Omnilert spokesperson previously told the Baltimore Banner that the company was reviewing the lawsuit and was “truly sorry for the fear they and their families experienced. We understand why they want answers.” A spokesperson for Baltimore county told the New York Times that the district cannot comment on pending litigation.
The lawsuit included texts from the school principal making light of the incident in messages to fellow administrators that contained emojis of a smiley face crying with laughter. The complaint said she did not apologize to the students.
One officer allegedly said as he began to leave the scene: “Fucking Omnialerts” and: “Stupid AI cameras.” His colleague allegedly joked to the plaintiffs: “Be careful on school property, especially holding stuff like that … be careful with your chips bags.”
The students didn’t find that funny, and reported feeling pain from tight handcuffs, as well as lasting emotional distress, according to the complaint.
Taki Allen said he no longer feels safe waiting for rides or hanging out at school after hours; he often pays for rides home to avoid waiting for rides from friends or family.
Freida Winfield, whose son Keith is part of the lawsuit, was en route to pick up him and his friends when they were detained. “ No child in Baltimore county should face this kind of danger while waiting outside his own school for a ride home from his mother,” said Winfield.

Bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.
Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Neon — bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.
Neon ranks ahead of comparable models and #3 overall with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level, landing just behind larger, slower models. On the Vals Index , Neon ranks #2 and lands on the Pareto frontier. Beyond just pushing on raw model capability, we’re continuing to make our models better to work with, Neon ranks #2 on steerability (adapting cleanly to mid-task user corrections) on the new Agent Arena Index . Neon also excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing.
The model is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.
Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out today in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio , Gemini for business (via API and model dropdown), for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , and for Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app .
Enterprise work lives in spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video. Neon can synthesize across all of these inputs in a single 1 million-token context window and turns inputs into structured deliverables. Independent evaluations rank Neon as one of the top models and on benchmarks like the Vals Index , it ranks #2 (70.9%), and reaches #1 on both the Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench .
Neon also shows strong wins across categories on Surge AI , ranking #1 on most benchmarks across finance, accounting, spreadsheet modeling, and complex constraint following. It also scores 73.5% on Chartography for reading dense professional charts and performs on par with leading models on Agents' Last Exam v1.1 (75.8%). It achieves #1 overall on both Zapier’s AutomationBench (56.3%) and Andon Labs' Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843), a long-horizon simulation of running a business. Finally, it debuts #2 globally with a score of 1336 on Arena's new Agent Arena Index across 4,200+ real-world agent sessions.
On scientific and mathematical reasoning, spanning quantitative analysis, mathematics, and technical research problems, Neon is best in class on Terminal-Bench Science (70.5%), RiemannBench (84.0%), and HLE-Diamond (71.3%).
Engineered for long-running agent workflows, Neon sustains performance through complex, tool-heavy tasks end-to-end — whether running standalone or acting as a fast, high-judgment Orchestrator directing parallel Hydrogen subagents in Google Antigravity. It cuts down on redundant file reads, shares progress as it works, and handles context compaction reliably in long sessions.
Across core developer and researcher workflows, Neon achieves frontier performance and is competitive with the leading models in its class, ranking #1 overall on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (58.6), with a score of 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2% (at its default high setting) on FrontierCode 2.0 . For production-ready code, Neon handles multi-file debugging and refactoring across repositories with targeted, surgical edits. On SWE-sweep, it already leads on the mini-SWE harness (12.8%) and more than triples to a state-of-the-art 39.0% in Google Antigravity showing what the Antigravity harness unlocks.
Driving Blender MCP in Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Neon used /swarm to build a photorealistic 3D lab bench visualizing the model names with elemental accuracy pairing Bunsen flames for Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen with high-voltage gas discharge tubes for Gemini 4 Argon and Neon.
In Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Neon wrote a first-person WebGL2 freeride ski simulator from scratch on real Mont Blanc and Chamonix elevation terrain — combining 10,200 lines of custom shaders, 120 Hz ski physics across six alpine lines, dynamic carved tracks, slab avalanches, and spatial Web Audio with zero pre-made assets.
Using /swarm in Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Neon pulled archival photos to recreate Alan Turing’s 1936 study at King’s College, Cambridge in interactive 3D — from King’s Chapel outside to Room X.8 inside, complete with a working Universal Turing Machine running on his desk.
In Google Antigravity, a Gemini 4 Neon agent swarm turned a single image into a 100,000-cell Google Sheet with zero embedded images and zero Apps Script — using over 500,000 live spreadsheet formulas to run edge detection, map 3D depth, and relight the scene across six interactive modes.
We’re refining thinking levels with each new model release to give teams finer control and a smoother progression from one tier to the next. Neon’s four levels scale steadily, letting teams dial intelligence and token spend to what each workload needs.
Neon delivers high performance at a lower cost per task across third-party benchmarks. At its default high thinking level, it pairs a high Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score with a 32% lower cost per task than Carbon. It also sits on the Pareto frontier on both the Vals index and Agent Arena at high, with roughly 50% to 80% lower cost per task than top competing frontier models. xhigh thinking adds deeper, multi-step reasoning for the hardest engineering, analytical, and scientific workloads. Neon shows its highest intelligence score here, while still costing 36%+ less per task than competing models at their highest setting.
As agentic coding scales, generating secure code from the start is critical. Gemini 4 Neon for cyber produces more secure code than Carbon across all easy, medium, and hard challenges on AutoBaxBench , achieving state-of-the-art on the hard tier (76%).
Securing systems also means proactively finding flaws before attackers do. Penetration testing has served as a cornerstone of enterprise cybersecurity. On WebExploitBench v1.2 , Neon is state-of-the-art (51.26%) at half the cost of competing large models.
To fortify existing code, Neon for cyber delivers frontier-level performance across the code hardening lifecycle — vulnerability finding, validating, and patching — all while being faster and more cost efficient than large frontier models.
Gemini 4 Neon for cyber is rolling out to trusted defenders in the coming days as part of the Fairwind Program .
Gemini 4 Neon builds on improvements from our Gemini 4 safety and security stack — maintaining Gemini 4 Carbon-level protections against severe misuse and prompt injection while advancing further on model alignment and agentic behavior. For a model meant to carry demanding, long-running work in production, we concentrated on:
In the Gemini app, Gemini 4 Neon excels at work that requires frontier-level reasoning and fast responses.
Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows. While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency. Neon delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.

During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age of AI-aided cyberattacks, are just waiting to be exploited.
“Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.”
In other words: The smartification of the economy, in which much of the world’s “dumb” devices were hooked up to the internet, is now causing tremendous headaches.
The conversation took place against the backdrop of a wave of recent large-scale outages — including one involving Microsoft Outlook. Others have involved the NSA, the FFA, and Apple. Concerns have swirled that these outages are the result of cyberattacks, although officials have denied those claims. Still, the reality of AI-aided cyberattacks is spurring companies to find new strategies for vulnerability discovery and remediation.
Nadella touched briefly on the recent Outlook situation, noting that the global inconvenience was the result of a “latent bug” that led to a “perfect storm.”
“We put out an incident response, and we’re going to obviously take all of the learnings, both upstream architectural, as well as operational, and fix that,” he added.
“Somebody was telling me about sort of even the transportation systems and the amount of stuff that’s discoverable but with unpatchable firmware,” Nadella also added on the topic of vulnerable systems. “So we’ll have to really modernize for sure … and then we will have to assess what the threat vector looks like, what our own ability to both detect and then defend in real time looks like.”
Nadella made a broader point as well, which is that the process of patching software vulnerabilities has escalated to match the speed of potential exploitation, but that this has caused more problems.
“We now have a very powerful tool that finds vulnerabilities,” he said. However, companies used to have more time to test those patches, understand a situation, and deploy them, he said. At the same time, AI has made sophisticated cyberattacks much easier to enact.
“The patch [now] needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild, right? So that’s going to create instability.”

GTA 6 için milyonlarca kişi oyun konsollarının başında bekliyor. Peki Grand Theft Auto (GTA) video oyunu neden nesiller boyunca bu kadar büyük bir heyecan yaratıyor?
GTA 6 adlı video oyununun piyasaya çıkışına birkaç gün kala yayımlanan son fragmanı böyleydi.
Meraklıları oyunu haftalar öncesinden bilgisayarlarına indirdi. Ve nihayet o gün geldi ve Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 kullanıma 19 Kasım'dan itibaren açılıyor.
Oyun konsollarının başına geçen milyonlarca kişi şimdi kriminal çift Jason ve Lucia ile birlikte, şık bir spor arabayla kurgusal ABD metropolü Vice City'de gaza basacak. Oyunun boyutu nedeniyle indirme işlemi, internet bağlantısına bağlı olarak günler sürebiliyor. İnternet sağlayıcıları son günlerde veri trafiğinde belirgin bir artış tespit etti.
Yıllardır eşi benzeri görülmemiş bir heyecanla beklenen GTA 6, şimdiden rekorlar kırıyor. Bugüne kadar hiçbir oyun bu kadar fazla ön sipariş verilmedi. Tahminlere göre yaklaşık on milyon kişi oyunu şimdiden satın aldı. GTA 6, abartısız söylemek gerekirse, küresel çapta bir kültür fenomeni hâline gelmiş durumda.
Oyunda GTA 6'nın kurgusal dünyasının esinlendiği Miami, Vice City'ye dönüşüyor. Miami kenti de bu esinlenmeden mutlu. Hatta NBA takımlarından Miami Heat, "Vice City" adı yazılı özel formalarla sahaya çıktı. Oyunun müziklerinde yer alan sanatçılar Miami'de düzenlenen festivallerde sahne alıyor. Pazarlama kampanyasının bir parçası olan "Vice City" tabelası da yol kenarlarına monte bile edildi.
Oyundan beklentiler büyük. Yaklaşık 5 bin kişi on yılı aşkın bir süre boyunca oyun üzerinde çalıştı. Geliştirme maliyetinin 1,5 milyar ABD dolarından fazla olduğu tahmin ediliyor.
Neu-Ulm Üniversitesi'nde kültür bilimci ve oyun tasarımı ile oyun çalışmaları profesörü olan Rudolf Thomas Inderst, "Yalnızca bu rakamlar nedeniyle ve elbette serinin son derece başarılı ve popüler geçmişi sayesinde, en azından çok büyük bir istisnai çıkıştan söz edebiliriz" diyor. Inderst'e göre, çok fazla emek harcanmış bir üründen insanların çok büyük beklentiler içinde olması son derece doğal. GTA 6, günümüzde oyunların oynanış, anlatım, görsellik ve teknik açıdan nelere kadir olduğunu gösterecek.
Video oyunu serisi neredeyse 30 yıldır var ve çıtayı sürekli olarak yükseltti. GTA, siyaset, kültür ve medyayı parodi konusu yapıyor, ABD toplumuna ve "Amerikan Rüyası'na" yönelik acımasız bir hiciv sunuyor. Seri ayrıca oyun özgürlüğünü temsil ediyor.
Oyuncular bu dünyada diledikleri her şeyi yapabiliyor: Bir helikopteri roketatarla düşürmek, berbere gitmek, sahilde yürüyüş yapmak, gece kulüplerini ziyaret etmek, araba yarışlarına katılmak ve daha fazlası.
Oyunla ilgili sıra dışı olan noktalardan biri de kurgusal dünyadaki tüm karakterlerin canlı görünmesi. GTA 6'da bu karakterler oyuncuların davranışlarına şahsına münhasır bir tepki veriyor. Kişiliklerine bağlı olarak örneğin daha korkak ya da daha saldırgan davranıyorlar. Oyunda yaklaşık 600 bin kişi animasyonu var.
GTA 6'nın dünyası yetişkinler için devasa bir oyun parkı. Y kuşağı GTA 3, GTA: Vice City, GTA: San Andreas ve GTA 4 ile büyüdü, Z kuşağı ise GTA 5 ile. Alfa kuşağı aslında GTA 6 için henüz çok genç ancak büyük olasılıkla oyunu yine de oynamanın bir yolunu bulacaklar.
Serinin özellikle GTA 5'in ve çok oyunculu türevi GTA Online'ın kalıcı başarısında, sosyal medyanın da kuşkusuz payı var. Çok sayıda içerik üreticisi oyun oturumlarını Twitch ya da YouTube'da yayınlıyor, özellikle komik oyun sahneleri TikTok'ta paylaşılıyor.
Öte yandan bazı oyuncular GTA dünyasında buluşuyor ve tutarlı biçimde kendilerine belirledikleri canlandırıyor. Örneğin taksi şoförü, yargıç ya da işsiz küçük çaplı suçlu rolüne bürünüyor ve karakterleri için inandırıcı arka plan hikâyeleri uyduruyorlar. Kimileri bunun için bir aksan bile ediniyor.
GTA 6'ya yönelik heyecan yalnızca oyunun kendisine fayda sağlamakla kalmayabilir, daha fazla insanı yeniden konsolların başına çekerek tüm oyun sektörüne de ivme kazandırabilir. Zira Covid-19 salgını sırasında yaşanan yükselişi, stüdyo kapanışları ve işten çıkarmalar izledi. Tahminlere göre, 2022'den bu yana dünya genelinde oyun sektöründen 50 binden fazla kişi işini kaybetti.
Ancak GTA'yı geliştiren stüdyo Rockstar'ın görkemli ürünleri ne kadar ayrıntıya düşkün olsa da hayranların takdir ettiği bu mükemmeliyetçiliğin gölge tarafları da var. Rockstar şirketi, diğer birçok oyun firması gibi, uzun yıllardır çalışma koşulları nedeniyle eleştiri konusu oluyor.
Kültür bilimci Rudolf Thomas Inderst, "Çalışanların içsel motivasyonunun bu kadar güçlü olduğu her yerde, sömürüye başvurmak da cazip hale geliyor" diyor.
Eski geliştiriciler aşırı çalışma saatlerini ve artık sağlıklı olmayan yüksek iş yükünü anlatıyor. Sendikacılar, yönetimin kendilerini gözetim altında tuttuğunu ve çalışmalarını sabote ettiğini öne sürüyor.
Oyunu geliştirenlere şimdi bir sendikanın tanınması için mücadele veriyor. Bu sendika, onlara çalışma saatleri, maaşlar, emeklilik planı ve ebeveyn izni düzenlemeleri gibi konularda söz sahibi olma imkânı sağlayacak. Başarılı olurlarsa bu, adil çalışma koşullarını sağlamakta çoğu zaman hâlâ zorlanan oyun sektörü için güçlü bir sinyal olacak.

Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk elaborated on his thoughts about Nvidia’s leadership change.
“Jensen is an old friend of mine,” Musk said. “I would call Jensen, you know, Michael Jordan at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team.”
On X, the social media platform he owns, Musk even said he would hire Huang.
“He’s one of the most talented entrepreneur-CEOs in history,” Musk said when asked about his X post. “Who wouldn’t want to hire Jensen?”
Musk also signed a petition , alongside over 200,000 other people, urging Nvidia to reinstate its former CEO. Nvidia’s board, however, confirmed it is not planning to bring Huang back.
“[It] doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me…,” Musk said of that decision. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.”
He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades,” Musk added. “He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him… and many of them are there because of him, and have higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.”
Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey also said that he thinks Nvidia is making the wrong decision by not reinstating Huang.
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said earlier in the day at the DealBook event. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”
Musk also did not express concern over what Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could mean for U.S. national security.
“I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders.”
Other peers in the industry, like Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , reaffirmed their faith in Nvidia to move forward without its founder and CEO of 33 years at the helm.
“It’s the Nvidia board’s decision, but I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella said at DealBook. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”

The MacBook Neo was already cheap, so Apple hasn't been eager to give much in the way of price cuts—despite the laptop having been out for seven months. But finally, the MacBook Neo's price has dropped by $50, bringing it down to $649. That's a great deal, especially if you're looking for an affordable laptop that feels premium, with a metal chassis and quality display. The 8 GB of RAM is limiting, but if your needs aren't overly heavy, the MacBook Neo should do the trick—especially at this price.
These days, you'll be hard-pressed to find a laptop for under $1,000 that doesn't have any major compromises. That's even more uncommon for a laptop with a larger screen. But the IdeaPad Slim 5x is just that. It's a 15-inch laptop with great performance, long-lasting battery life, lots of ports, a solid trackpad, and a high-resolution OLED screen. It even comes packed to the brim with 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage. It's not as thin as the 15-inch MacBook Air, no, but then again, it's hundreds of dollars cheaper.
It might be well over two years old, but I still find myself recommending the Surface Laptop from 2024. The price is down to $900 right now, which is a good deal for these specs, performance, and battery life. You're limited to only the blue color option, but it's the best price I've seen on this laptop this year so far. My favorite feature will always be the 3:2 aspect ratio screen, which gives the display a taller shape for more vertical space to work with.
There is a newer version , which comes with the Snapdragon X2 Plus/Elite chips, but I've found that it's still quite expensive. The IdeaPad Slim 5x listed above is the better option if you're OK with a larger device, since it uses those next-generation Snapdragon chips (for less money). But if you're sold on the design of the Surface Laptop, this is the one to get.
With the MacBook Neo selling for $649, you might look at something like the HP OmniBook 5 with suspicion. Even on sale for $750, being $100 more than the MacBook Neo doesn't seems like a great position to be in for an entry-level Windows laptop. And while this laptop is on sale often, this is $100 cheaper than I've seen it over the past few weeks.
The HP OmniBook 5 is a special device, with its OLED display, very thin chassis, and 16 GB of RAM. It very much looks like a laptop that should cost hundreds more. Battery life is great too, thanks to the Snapdragon X chip inside. The 16 GB of RAM is still the main selling point here—if it was any less, I would recommend the XPS 13 in nearly every scenario (but it's not on sale right now). It's only real downfall is the touchpad. It feels frustratingly clumsy one to use, making precise movements difficult.

Ukraine’s strike used homegrown tech while adapting battlefield lessons from its adversary.
A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in.
On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile.
The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities.
During the Ukrainian attacks on the Kerch Strait Bridge, the flying mesh network allowed operators located more than 250 kilometers away (155 miles) to remotely guide missiles and drones in evading Russian air defenses while also homing in on the bridge’s weakest structural points, according to the Financial Times .
Ukraine’s takedown of the bridge segment was preceded by weeks of preparatory strikes that systematically destroyed or degraded Russian air defense weapons, radars and electronic warfare equipment arrayed to protect the bridge. The November 15 night attack on the bridge also coincided with the largest Ukrainian overnight drone attack on Russia since the start of the full-scale war, Reuters reported .
Notably, Ukraine conducted the coordinated strike with primarily Ukrainian developed or adapted technologies. The Financial Times reported that “Ukrainian units involved in the operation deliberately avoided using Starshield, the military version of Musk’s Starlink satellite network,” because of recent US restrictions that prevent Ukraine from using Starshield on drones or anything else traveling more than 100 miles per hour (161 kilometers per hour).
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the latest US-imposed restrictions on Starshield have not yet been lifted , although SpaceX denied that the restrictions had returned. Zelenskyy described the speed limit as interfering with some Ukrainian drone interceptor technologies that were designed to defend against Russian drones attacking Ukrainian cities and infrastructure .
However, the Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Strait Bridge provide yet another example of how the Ukrainian military and defense technology companies have been learning to fight without relying on Starlink . This is also not the first time that Ukraine, arguably the leading country in developing new battlefield uses of drones , has adopted a Russian battlefield innovation for its own uses.
From Russia’s view, the only glimmer of good news may be that the bridge’s railway section was only moderately damaged. The Ukrainian newspaper Kyiv Independent pointed to Russian news and video sources indicating that trains appeared to be running again on the bridge after the strikes.
But the severe damage to the bridge’s arch and roadway section cuts off a crucial transportation and supply link between Russia and the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula of Ukraine. The Institute for the Study of War assesses that the “destruction of the bridge” will complicate Russia’s ability to maintain its occupation and military basing within the peninsula.
The other overland supply route between Russia and Crimea involves highways running through Russian-occupied southern Ukraine. But Ukrainian forces have already been striking such highway infrastructure and the Russian supply trucks running along the exposed route.
Fallen debris from the bridge’s collapsed arch may also prevent any large ship traffic from passing through the Kerch Strait that connects the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea, according to a Telegram channel owner based in Crimea. That makes it even more difficult for Russia to resupply the Crimean peninsula by sea—and Ukrainian drones have previously struck dozens of Russian ships in the Sea of Azov .
Beyond the physical damage to the bridge, such attacks represent a symbolic blow to Putin’s ambition of holding onto the Crimean peninsula. After Russian forces seized Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, Russia based much of its Black Sea Fleet at the naval base in Sevastopol and later used the peninsula as a logistics hub for its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The $3.5 billion Kerch Strait Bridge was built as a physical link to cement Russia’s claim over Crimea. Putin personally drove a construction truck across the bridge to commemorate its opening in 2018. He repeated the bridge-crossing feat in a Mercedes in December 2022, after a Ukrainian truck bomb attack temporarily damaged the bridge in October of that year.
In 2025, the bridge was damaged again after Ukraine’s Security Service used agents to plant mines under the bridge supports. Again, Russia repaired the damage.
The Kerch Strait Bridge’s future prospects look much bleaker now following the latest missile and drone strikes. The bridge was initially constructed in two years, and engineering experts told The New York Times that repairs to the bridge roadway could also take two years under normal circumstances. But they also agreed that any damage to the bridge’s piers could extend that repair time—and Russian repair efforts would likely be at risk from future Ukrainian missile and drone attacks.

Google is trying to force Gemini on schools, and they’re not thrilled.
New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times . Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”
Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times , New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”
In a statement to The Verge , Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”
Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills , and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests . There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age . But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago
Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro , to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.
Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.
Speaking outside the recently reopened US embassy in Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, on Wednesday, Hegseth said: “It’s a great honor to be here as the first United States secretary of war this century to set foot in Venezuela.​ Just one year ago my presence here … would have been deemed impossible, almost unimaginable.
“In fact, exactly one year ago today … [Maduro] stood on a stage not too far from here and yelled mockingly, ‘Come and get me!’” Hegseth recalled, before adding sarcastically: “Well, we answered that call.
“The reality is that … January 3 is the day that will go down in history as a day of liberation for Venezuela,” Hegseth claimed, although Maduro’s allies continue to hold power with US support.
Earlier in the day, Hegseth was welcomed to the Miraflores Palace by Maduro’s former vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez , who became acting president with Donald Trump’s blessing after his abduction.
In the aftermath of the deadly US attack, Hegseth was one of the bluntest Trump administration voices when it came to celebrating the invasion. “Maduro had his chance … he effed around and he found out,” the defense secretary bragged .
Speaking at the palace, Hegseth struck a more conciliatory tone as he vowed to deepen cooperation with Venezuela’s new leaders in brief comments that were broadcast by the state broadcaster VTV.
“I stand here on behalf of President Trump, who sends his greeting and looks forward to the opportunities, not just militarily … but also economically: the incredible resource capabilities that your country has, that we look forward to unlocking together with you,” Hegseth told Rodríguez and senior cabinet members, including the defense and foreign ministers, Gustavo González López and Oliver Blanco.
Hegseth said his visit to Rodríguez’s “beautiful country” was designed to re-establish and increase “defense cooperation” between “two great militaries” that less than a year ago were briefly at war. Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Trump officials were trying to negotiate a long-term US troop presence in Venezuela as part of their push for regional hegemony.
“I appreciate your leadership and commitment to your country,” Hegseth told Maduro’s successor, a once outspoken anti-imperialist leftist who has overseen an unlikely realignment with Washington since her ally was grabbed.
During her five-minute address, Rodríguez, whose oil-rich country is widely seen to have become a US protectorate after January’s invasion, made no mention of Maduro, who is behind bars in New York City.
But referring indirectly to his capture and the subsequent reconciliation with Washington, she told Hegseth: “Thanks to the political and geopolitical maturity of our governments, we have – in a very short period of time, just a few months – turned what were very difficult and very tough times for our people, into an extraordinary space for cooperation and mutual benefit.”
Rodríguez hailed the “historic” energy deal her government recently struck with Trump, who has called it “the biggest oil deal in world history” as well as “the spoils” of his “conquest” of Venezuela.
Hegseth claimed the agreement, which reportedly involves 65bn barrels of reserves, “makes the strait of Hormuz a non-factor for the western hemisphere”.
Critics of Rodríguez’s political movement painted Hegseth’s visit as a humiliating act of genuflection for a president with no choice but to roll out the red carpet for the man whose troops captured her boss.
Writing on X, Luz Mely Reyes, a prominent Venezuelan journalist, said Hegseth’s visit was designed to underscore Washington’s “direct administration” of her country.
“Ten months after Nicolás Maduro’s capture, Washington no longer needs to fire shots to remind everyone who is in charge: the mere presence on Venezuelan soil of the architect of the January incursion reaffirms that the country’s operational sovereignty is subject to the White House’s directives,” Reyes said.
Reyes suspected the visit also carried a message for members of Venezuela’s armed forces. “Domestically, the trip forces the military high command to legitimize the man who directed the extraction of their former commander in chief,” she said. “In this regard, I wonder whether it might be a message of discipline intended to prevent any pockets of resistance in the barracks.”
Trump’s attempts to expand his Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition of Latin American governments suffered a major blow last month with the defeat of his far-right ally, Flávio Bolsonaro, in Brazil’s presidential election. The leftwing winner, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has indicated his country will not join the initiative.
But Venezuela’s interim government is in little position to resist. During his surprise visit to Venezuela, Hegseth said Venezuela had gone from being “our most aggressive regional threat to [being] a compliant security partner”. He praised Rodríguez for working “closely, pragmatically, and diligently with the United States to stabilize Venezuela”. Hegseth claimed US and Venezuelan armed forces would work together to attack “narco-terrorists” operating on Venezuelan soil, vowing: “We will hunt you down. We will find you. And we will kill you.”
Concluding her speech at the palace, Rodríguez told her foe-turned-friend: “Thank you, secretary, and I wish you a lifetime of happiness.”

United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has announced a new agreement with Venezuela’s interim government to facilitate military cooperation between the two countries.
The Pentagon chief made a surprise visit to the Venezuelan capital of Caracas on Wednesday, becoming the latest in a series of high-level officials under US President Donald Trump to travel to the South American country.
During his stop, Hegseth revealed that the deal would include intelligence sharing and joint training for the two countries’ militaries.
“We see this as a reestablishment of our defence partnership and the opportunity to work together between our two great militaries,” he said.
Their shared aim would be “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all”, Hegseth added.
Hegseth was hosted by interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who has led the government since her swearing-in on January 5. His trip was not previously announced by the Pentagon.
The Trump administration has exerted heavy influence over Rodriguez and her government after abducting former President Nicolas Maduro during a military attack on January 3.
Rodriguez was previously Venezuela’s vice president. Trump has justified the attack as a law enforcement effort designed to force Maduro to “stand trial on American soil”, charging him with weapons- and drug-related crimes.
After the operation, Trump also said he planned to “run” Venezuela, and he told The Atlantic magazine that Rodriguez could “pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro” if she refuses to comply with US demands.
Since then, he has worked with the Venezuelan government to extract concessions on US priorities such as energy development and military cooperation.
Critics have accused the US of reducing Venezuela to a vassal state and exploiting its resources while leaving Maduro’s government largely intact.
Under Maduro, the Venezuelan state was accused of human rights abuses including torture, arbitrary imprisonment and extrajudicial killings.
Still, Trump has held up Venezuela as a model he would like to see replicated in other countries, like Iran and Cuba.
In Wednesday’s remarks, Hegseth said that the South American country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”.
Rodriguez hailed the agreement as a “resumption of the technical-military relationship between both countries”, and she expressed hope that their cooperation could be “brought to its highest possible level”.
Hegseth is also set to meet with officials in Colombia later on Wednesday as part of a trip to the region.
Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora said on Tuesday that the US would deliver a C-130 Hercules military aircraft, as the US steps up military involvement across Latin America.
Hegseth has faced pressure to step down from his role, following a midterm election in which the US-Israel war on Iran contributed to Republican losses across the country.
A key member of Trump’s cabinet, Hegseth has championed the war, as well as efforts to weaken rules of engagement designed to limit civilian casualties.
Hegseth narrowly avoided a recent impeachment effort in the US Congress this month. The sponsor of that effort, outgoing Republican US Representative Thomas Massie, cited the Iran war as well as a campaign of military strikes targeting alleged drug trafficking vessels off the coast of Latin America.
The boat-strike campaign has killed an estimated 244 people and has been denounced as extrajudicial killings by legal experts.

Israeli tanks advance beyond the ‘Yellow Line’, forcing Palestinians to flee again as Gaza faces a deepening humanitarian crisis.
Israeli forces have launched a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire and forcing Palestinian families, many of whom had already been displaced, to flee their homes once again.
The operation, the first major ground offensive publicly announced by the Israeli military since the ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, follows a warning by the United States-backed Board of Peace that the 13-month-old agreement risks collapse. In a report to the United Nations Security Council, the board accused Israel of restricting aid and delaying the deployment of Palestinian police, and Hamas of continuing armed activity and taxing goods entering Gaza. Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”.
Israeli tanks and bulldozers advanced towards Salah al-Din Street, Gaza’s main north-south route, east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and north of the Bureij refugee camp, Al Jazeera correspondents reported. Palestinians fled those areas, amid heavy gunfire and artillery shelling.
The Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territory, known as COGAT, said the army had closed that stretch of Salah al-Din Street and told residents to stay away until further notice. The army hasn’t said how long the operation will last.
An Israeli attack on al-Mughraqa killed one person and wounded several others, an official at al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera. Separate attacks in Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City killed three more people.
“We fear this may be the start of a broader operation and that displacement will begin anew, as we have not yet recovered from the effects of the previous war and displacement,” Mahmoud al-Saafin, a 27-year-old resident of Bureij, told the AFP news agency.
The areas targeted in the operation lie west of the “Yellow Line”, where Israeli troops pulled back to under the first phase of President Donald Trump’s plan, leaving them in about 53 percent of Gaza. Israel has, however, continued to move that line gradually, and it now encompasses around two-thirds of the enclave. More than two million Palestinians live in the rest, mostly in tents.
The military told AFP it had launched “a precise operation” west of the line “to remove a threat” posed to the Israeli army, adding that “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area, adding it was responding to Hamas ceasefire violations.
“We reserve the freedom to act and manoeuvre whenever necessary to eliminate any immediate threat in the Gaza Strip,” the army said.
Israel says Hamas has been regrouping and rearming, and it has stepped up attacks. On Saturday, an Israeli attack killed Samir Abu Younis, the Qassam Brigades’ Rafah commander.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel won’t withdraw until Hamas is dismantled. “If tensions escalate on the various fronts, we are fully prepared to seize additional territory, evacuate local residents and incorporate it into Israel’s permanent security perimeter,” he said.
Hamas called the operation and the forced evacuations northeast of Nuseirat “a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement”, and urged mediators to “intervene immediately”.
It accused Israel of “systematically” squeezing Palestinians into a narrow area of Gaza, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s caretaker government of escalating to escape its domestic crises.
Hamas also condemned the Board of Peace for having “unacceptably equated the occupation’s ongoing aggression with the suffering of the Palestinian victim”.
The Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine called the operation a “prelude” to a wider escalation aimed at forcibly displacing Palestinians.
Israeli forces have kept up near-daily attacks, shelling and home demolitions. Gaza’s Ministry of Health says they have killed 1,658 Palestinians and wounded 6,000 since the ceasefire began. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed in the same period, the Reuters news agency reports.
On Tuesday alone, Israeli fire killed six Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, Gaza’s civil defence agency and hospitals told AFP.
Aid remains restricted. About 100,000 tents are waiting to enter Gaza, held up by crossing closures and lengthy Israeli security checks, the International Organization for Migration says.
The ceasefire halted major fighting, but the rest of the plan, covering Israel’s withdrawal, reconstruction and Hamas’s disarmament, has stalled. Hamas agreed in July to a roadmap to give up its weapons and hand over governance. Israel rejected it.
Israel also hasn’t let the board’s technocratic administration start work in Gaza. That has held up an international stabilisation force, The Associated Press news agency reported.
The board spelled out what failure would mean. “Should it collapse, there would be no road map to return to, no administration to deploy and no enabling environment to rebuild.”

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela on Wednesday, state TV reported, during an unexpected visit to Caracas.
Hegseth was received by Venezuela's interim leader, Delcy Rodríguez, in the capital ahead of a planned visit to Colombia later Wednesday.
"We see this as a renewal of our defence partnership and an opportunity for our two great armed forces to work together," Hegseth said, according to footage broadcast by VTV, Venezuela's state television channel.
The trip, which had not been publicly announced by the Pentagon, marks another step in the rapprochement between Washington and Caracas following the capture in January of Nicolás Maduro.
The cooperation agreement announced by Hegseth and Rodríguez provides for the resumption of technical and military cooperation between Washington and Caracas, which had been suspended for years amid deteriorating diplomatic relations between the two countries.
According to the Venezuelan leader, one of the main objectives is to strengthen the training of Venezuelan armed forces personnel through joint training and cooperation programmes. Rodríguez said the initiative would help improve the military's preparedness to respond to shared threats.
The agreement also aims to improve the operational equipment available to Venezuelan forces and provide access to new technologies. So far, neither government has provided details on the timeline for implementing the agreement, the resources to be allocated or the specific mechanisms through which cooperation will take place.
Rodríguez took power after Maduro was captured, although her continued leadership of the country remains shrouded in uncertainty. Her interim mandate expired in July and there is still no announced date for the next presidential election.
The rapprochement between Washington and Caracas has also been marked by agreements over Venezuelan oil and by the United States' strategy against drug trafficking in the Caribbean and the Pacific, which has caused the deaths of at least 240 people since September 2025 in attacks on vessels suspected of carrying drugs.
Hegseth's visit is part of efforts by Donald Trump's administration to expand its influence in Venezuela. The defence secretary is the third member of Trump's cabinet to travel to the country this year, following trips by the interior and energy secretaries, focused on Venezuela's oil and mineral resources.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.
Embattled US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced appearance in Caracas on Wednesday, the highest-level US visit since the January ouster of president Nicolas Maduro .
During the surprise stopoff en route to Colombia , Hegseth announced renewed US-Venezuelan military cooperation and vowed to "hunt" down drug traffickers.
"We will hunt you down, we will find you, and we will kill you," he said after announcing the deal that marks a dramatic thaw in long-hostile relations.
"You will no longer export your crime and your misery to America, to Venezuela , or any other country in the region," he added, referring to "narco-terrorists."
Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez hailed a "resumption of the technical-military relationship between both countries" after years of rupture and US sanctions .
She has governed Venezuela with Washington's backing since US special forces captured Maduro and spirited him to New York , where he faces trial on charges of "narco-terrorism."
Read more Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro and wife Cilia Flores deny US torture charges as 'false accusations'
The American embrace of Maduro's former vice president has not gone down well among the country's often-repressed pro-democracy opposition.
While Venezuelans enjoy more freedoms than a year ago, US President Donald Trump 's administration has allowed swaths of the authoritarian state apparatus to remain in place.
Hundreds of political prisoners remain behind bars and no date has been set for free and fair elections .
But Venezuela is seen as vital for US efforts to secure new sources of oil, isolate Cuba 's communist government and curb cocaine trafficking from South America.
Caracas has long been accused of harboring Colombian drug-running guerrilla groups including the ELN, which operate across vast tracts of territory on either side of the border.
Hegseth, who recently avoided congressional impeachment and faces sustained scrutiny for his handling of the Iran war and the legality of deadly anti-drug strikes, later traveled to the Colombian capital Bogota.
Read more Rubio kicks off tour in Latin America as US vies for regional influence
Since Trump returned to office two years ago, the United States has significantly escalated military operations in Latin America.
US forces have struck alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, killing more than 230 people, according to an AFP tally.
Rights groups say Trump's administration has provided scant proof that the vessels had anything to do with drug trafficking , warning that the strikes may amount to extrajudicial killings.
Washington has deployed troops, powerful Reaper drones and other military assets to the region.
AFP uncovered at least 20 US military flights to an isolated base on Ecuador 's Pacific coast, including C-130 Hercules and C-17 Globemaster transport planes, V-22 Osprey tiltrotor aircraft and Black Hawk helicopters.
Satellite imagery shows the base undergoing significant construction work in recent months.
The US has also backed anti-narcotic strikes in Colombia , where Hegseth landed on Wednesday.
Washington and Bogota have long counted each other as allies in the war on drugs, with one governing the world's biggest cocaine market and the other its largest producer.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has sought to deepen the relationship even further since his inauguration in August, boosting military cooperation with the US and bombing drug-running guerrillas.
More than 300 US soldiers recently took part in anti-drug-trafficking exercises in the country alongside 400 Colombian soldiers.
Defence Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora, who greeted Hegseth in Bogota, announced the visit on Tuesday along with the delivery of a C-130 military aircraft.
The defense secretary's trip follows an impeachment attempt by Congress that threatened his job less than two years into his tenure.
Analysts say that when the Democratic majority is sworn in in January, Trump's policies and his Latin American alliances will come under fierce examination.

The US, Chinese and Russian leaders are to hold their first three-way talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold a three-way meeting on Thursday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, the first ever between the leaders of the world’s three most powerful militaries.
The meeting, which will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, has drawn comparisons with the 1945 wartime Yalta conference at which the United States, United Kingdom and then-Soviet Union agreed on the post-war order. But those powers had been allied during a world war. Analysts say the three men meeting on Thursday are arriving with very different goals, and that few concrete outcomes can be expected.
“It’s a summit of Trump’s ego, Putin’s tactics, China’s strategy,” Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera.
The trilateral meeting is taking place on the sidelines of the APEC leaders’ summit, which China is hosting in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. Trump travelled to China after attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations ( ASEAN ) meeting in Manila.
The White House has said that Trump plans to discuss the war with Iran as well as a possible three-way agreement on nuclear armament with Xi and Putin. Ukraine is not expected to be on the formal agenda, as Xi is understood to be reluctant to be drawn into what he views as a European matter.
The meeting comes as Trump has strained ties with traditional US allies, at times floating troop withdrawals from South Korea and cuts to assistance for Japan, while his administration continues to describe China as Washington’s main geopolitical rival.
Vuk Vuksanovic, a lecturer in foreign policy and grand strategy at the Department of War Studies, King’s College, London, cautioned against viewing the summit as a new “carve-up” of the world order, however.
“It is a far cry from being a new Yalta,” he said. “In Yalta, you actually had the idea about how the world was going to look, and where the demarcation line would potentially be between the superpowers. We don’t have anything similar, not even the contours of that, in the making at this moment.”
At the Yalta Conference in February 1945, US President Franklin D Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Crimea to shape the post-war order, agreeing on the division of Germany and setting the stage for Soviet influence over Eastern Europe.
Trump landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday, with Xi greeting him at the airport. This is their third in-person meeting since they paused their bitter trade war late last year. At its height, US trade tariffs on Chinese goods reached 145 percent, with China retaliating with tariffs of 125 percent on US goods, before a temporary truce agreed in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025, when tariffs were relaxed. Xi also agreed to pause new restrictions on exports of some rare earth metals which are crucial for manufacturing technology from smartphones to fighter jets. Soon after that, Trump relaxed restrictions on the sale of some Nvidia AI-related computer chips to China.
The truce has since been extended to January 10, 2027 to allow for broader trade talks.
China’s rare earth mineral exports to the US are still about 75 percent below normal levels, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
A scandal over Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China in breach of US export controls, has also strained ties, as has the recent scandal over Nvidia’s former CEO, Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs, including with a woman the US has accused of spying for China.
Beijing rejects all spying allegations as “baseless”, and Trump has said he does not plan to raise the issue at this meeting.
Expectations are low for a major thawing, however: Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation, told Al Jazeera that a handshake without incident would be seen as a win.
Trump’s special envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, have brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11, the first in direct format since February. The pair have visited both Kyiv and Moscow to promote these talks in recent days.
Days before they travelled to Moscow on Thursday last week, Trump said Washington and Moscow were close to a “big, beautiful agreement” covering not just Ukraine but “all of Europe”.
Trump’s rhetoric towards Putin has softened greatly in recent months, as it has hardened against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, whom he has publicly admonished for targeting Russian energy facilities, driving up the global cost of oil and diesel. Trump has also called for Zelenskyy to step down and has paused some sanctions on Russian oil, much to the anger of many in his Republican Party .
Some analysts are concerned that US negotiators may offer Russia concessions on NATO in return for peace, including pushing a deal that allows Russia to retain land it has seized from Ukraine in the past four years – a prospect that alarms European leaders.
China has become Russia’s top trading partner since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, weeks after the two had declared a “no limits” partnership.
At a summit in Beijing in May this year, Xi and Putin signed more than 40 cooperation agreements and hailed growing energy trade.
Russian oil exports to China rose 35 percent in the first quarter of 2026, according to a Kremlin aide. China has also ignored Western demands to stop supplying high-tech components to Russia’s weapons industry.
Chinese President Xi Jinping called for China and Russia to “lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world” after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Putin addressed the summit after Xi. He described Western powers as “former hegemons” and said Europe was experiencing a “humiliating decline”.
Analysts say Trump is the leader most eager to walk away with something he can present as a “win” from this trilateral meeting.
Vuksanovic said Trump is arriving “wounded domestically” following his Republican Party’s crushing defeat at the US midterm elections, which have seen the Democratic Party gain control of both US Houses of Congress. Trump’s legacy, Vuksanovic added, has been damaged by the war on Iran, particularly in light of Trump’s pledge not to drag the US into another “forever war” during his presidential campaign in 2024.
The deadlock that currently exists between the US and Iran has been described as a “ frozen war ” by observers.
“[Trump] hopes that he can get some quick-fix deal on something, at least, which he can then try to spin and sell to his base in the US as an enormous accomplishment,” Vuksanovic said. But he added that he doubts Trump could secure anything beyond “something very symbolic”, noting that the agenda of the meeting has remained opaque.
One issue Trump may push for is a trilateral agreement on nuclear armament. The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) between Russia and the US lapsed in February. It was first signed in 2010 and caps US and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals.
Trump previously rejected Russia’s proposal to extend the treaty after it expired, demanding instead a “new, improved and modernised” deal that includes Beijing. However, Xi is understood to be unenthusiastic about joining a treaty that China had no part in writing.
Lucas said Trump is there largely “for the photo opportunity”. But he drew a distinction between Trump and his administration, which he said wants to “regain their footing a little bit in terms of leadership” on China.

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.
His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the Senate also being under Democrats' control.
Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".
As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority. Seven races from the recent midterm elections are still uncalled.
Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.
The Congressional Black Caucus, currently made up of only Democratic House members, noted the potential history-making moment when Jeffries takes the helm of the House.
"The American people, largely driven by turnout among Black communities, particularly across the south, have trusted us to make Washington work for them," said the committee's chair, Yvette Clarke, in a statement. "Now, it is our charge and responsibility to do all we can to deliver on their faith."
Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote , Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from new members in the party's left wing, who have said the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.
"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.
All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.
President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.
Trump's opposition could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.
At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged that House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".
Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs .
Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.
The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".
Along with shepherding legislation, Jeffries as Speaker will also have to manage the complex array of investigations that Democrats plan to launch into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that they have regained control of the chamber's oversight powers.
Rounding out their party leadership team, House Democrats also elected Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as majority leader, Pete Aguilar of California as majority whip, and Joe Neguse of Colorado as assistant speaker.

Hakeem Jeffries is one step closer to making history as the first Black Speaker of the US House of Representatives, after Democrats nominated him for the powerful role despite a small but vocal group of progressive dissenters.
Jeffries, who has served as House minority leader and leader of the House Democratic Caucus since 2023, secured the nod following a closed-door vote. 251 voted for his nomination, compared with 11 against. The move came ahead of a full House vote when the new Congress convenes in January.
Many of those who voted “no” are a group of progressive newcomers, who said in a statement that there is “still work to be done” to ensure their priorities.
Jeffries, who hails from New York, ran unopposed but says he is taking nothing for granted. He faces a restive party eager for a change after voters ousted Republicans in a rebuke of President Donald Trump and his underlings.
Speaking after his nomination was announced, he vowed to "hold the crooks accountable", referring to Democratic plans to reverse Republican policies and investigate controversial moves by the Trump administration.
"We're going to fight to make sure that, in the face of the unprecedented corruption, chaos, and cruelty visited upon the American people, that House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones, because the American people deserve better," Jeffries told reporters.
His fighting talk came after Democrats unveiled plans for wide-ranging investigations into Trump officials and his business interests when they take control of the House in January.
On Wednesday, Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, sent 12 letters warning members of Trump's family and senior administration figures to preserve documents ahead of investigations into alleged corruption, immigration abuses and the handling of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
