IAEA chief Rafael Grossi has said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."
United Nations (UN) nuclear watchdog chief Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday North Korea has built an extension on its original uranium-enrichment plant at the Yongbyon nuclear complex.
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has been unable to access North Korea since Pyongyang expelled its inspectors in 2009. It now relies primarily on satellite imagery to monitor the country's nuclear activity.
Grossi addressed the ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Yongbyon and Kangson during a quarterly meeting of the IAEA's Board of Governors.
Kangson lies just southwest of Pyongyang, while the much larger Yongbyon facility is located farther north of the capital.
"Since ​mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original ​Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by ​late October 2026," Grossi said, with no further details.
He said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."
Enriched uranium is used as fuel for nuclear power plants and the nuclear reactors that run naval ships and submarines. It can also be used in nuclear weapons.
US President Donald Trump floated the possibility of a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as he went to China to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Meanwhile, North Korean state media — which typically operates behind the global news cycle — has only released images of Kim visiting a ski resort and Mount Paektu, making no mention of possible Shenzhen travel plans.
Kim has said he aims to arm the nation with an expansive nuclear force to counter the US and South Korea.
In March, soon after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, Kim accused Washington of "global terrorism and aggression."
The Iran war reinforced North Korea's long-standing view that it needs a nuclear arsenal to be able to defend itself against what it sees as its two largest enemies, South Korea and the US.
North Korea has been subject to various international sanctions over its nuclear weapons development and use of ballistic missile technology. But Pyongyang has repeatedly flouted the restrictions.
In September 2024, North Korea revealed its first covert uranium-enrichment plant. Kim delivered a speech then, including a call for "exponentially" expanding the country's nuclear arsenal.
In April, Grossi told reporters that his agency had confirmed "a rapid increase” in activities at nuclear facilities in North Korea.
In September, the IAEA passed resolutions at its annual conference regarding concerns about the North Korean nuclear program.
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of Kim Jong Un, said in response that the country's nuclear-armed status was "absolute."

Chelsea Women vs Paris Saint-Germain Women. Women's Champions League.
Match report as Chelsea snatched a late 1-0 win against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League; Veerle Buurman bundled her effort home from close range in the 88th minute; Chelsea now move to the top of the Champions League table with one league phase game to play
Veerle Buurman's late winner snatched a late 1-0 win for Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain to move them to the top of the Champions League table.
Sonia Bompastor's side looked as if they were heading to back-to-back goalless draws, following the 0-0 draw with BK Hacken last time out in Europe, until Buurman was able to bundle her effort home at the near post in the 88th minute.
The hosts had been the dominant side throughout but were thwarted by Katarzyna Kiedrzynek on more than one occasion.
Alyssa Thompson had come close to breaking the deadlock just before the break after seeing her initial shot and follow-up effort smothered by Kiedrzynek.
The corner for Buurman's timely winner arrived after the PSG goalkeeper got down well to her right to keep Sjoeke Nusken's header out.
Lucy Bronze's delivery and a slight touch on the way through sparked panic among the PSG defence and it was Buurman who reacted first to sweep home the winner, sending her side to the top of the table with one league phase game to go.
The Blues remain unbeaten in Europe, winning three of their five games so far, and are well placed to qualify for the last 16 through the top four automatic qualification spots. They face OH Leuven in their final game, where they will go into it as strong favourites.
"I like the resilience from my team. Believing until the end of the game we could score that important goal and it was really important for us to win tonight.
"What I like in my team and squad is the fact they are really flexible; they are really open-minded to changing systems sometimes, adapting to what is happening on the pitch.
"They understand really quickly. I think it was good for us to be able to change, to go to a back four. We wanted to have the width to destabilise them more than we did in the first half."
On her side potentially finishing in the top four: "We knew we had two games left and getting two wins will help us to probably secure top four.
"So we still have things under control and that was why it was really important for us to win."
"It was really important we scored the goal. Winning and three points was really important, especially after the last Champions League game where we drew against Hacken.
"A good team performance. We tried really hard and that I can score a goal is really important for the team."
"We spoke about it before the game about wanting to finish the evening on top. We are in a good spot going into the last game.
"It was a massive win. It was tough for us tonight. They defended really well and they're aggressive.
"It was a difficult game physically but to get the win was really important. Hopefully it will push us into the top four."
43: SO CLOSE! Thompson has an initial shot and a second effort saved by Kiedrzynek from close range.
53: SAVE! Kanjinga makes space to shoot, but Hampton keeps her effort out at the near post.
67: CLOSE! Buurman meets the corner and glances her header towards goal but it is saved by Kiedrzynek again.
86: ANOTHER SAVE! Nusken's header looks destined for the bottom corner until Kiedrzynek dives to claw it away.
87: GOAL! Chelsea finally break the deadlock as Buurman scores late winner at the near post.
texts.https://www.theguardian.com/football/202:
Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.
Buurman had stolen the show in Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match, and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.
“She is a top, young talent and is so mature on and off the pitch,” said Sonia Bompastor. “She is a confident player and a really complete player.”
Bompastor’s side were frustrated by Häcken last week, held to a 0-0 draw by the Swedish side and falling out of the top four automatic qualification places. There was a desire to put things right at AFC Wimbledon’s stadium and they did just that, albeit in not the prettiest of encounters.
“Sometimes in football you need to find a way to win and the result tonight was really important for us,” said Bompastor.
Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw both scored off the bench to earn Manchester City a 2-0 Women’s Champions League victory over Häcken in Gothenburg.
The first half ended goalless with City's best chances coming just before the break. Aoba Fujino was put through on goal but she hit her effort straight at Häcken keeper Jennifer Falk, who made saves from Grace Clinton and Rebecca Knaak to keep the hosts on terms at the interval.
Hemp and Shaw were both introduced at half-time by Andrée Jeglertz, and the England winger opened the scoring after 55 minutes. It was a fortuitous breakthrough, with Emma Östlund's clearance ricocheting off Hemp's shin and into the net [pictured]. Mary Fowler appeared to have added a second soon after, but her strike was ruled out for offside against Yui Hasegawa.
Soon after Hemp was denied her second goal when her shot hit the post, she turned creator by passing to an onrushing Shaw, who tucked home for City's second in the 77th minute. The visitors could have had a third, but Falk saved Fowler's stoppage-time penalty after a VAR intervention.
Signe Bruun also made the difference off the bench on Wednesday, scoring two late goals as Real Madrid wore down 10-woman Internazionale to win 3-1. The Danish forward put Madrid ahead five minutes of time before adding a late penalty to secure all three points.
Lineth Beerensteyn got the hosts off the mark in Madrid after 28 minutes, and Inter faced an uphill battle after Karolina Vilhjalmsdottir was sent off three minutes before the break. The visitors got an unexpected equaliser when Michela Cambiaghi headed in from a corner, and held on until Bruun's late double.
City and Real Madrid are both unbeaten after five league phase games, winning two and drawing three matches each as they bid to finish in the top four and avoid the playoffs. Juventus join them on nine points after late goals from Annamaria Serturini and Matilde Pavan earned a 2-0 home win over Leuven . PA and Guardian sport
PSG had lost 2-1 at home to Bayern Munich after three draws and one win in the competition before their trip to London. Denied a point late on, they remain 10th and dangerously close to slipping out of the playoff places with one game to play.
Chelsea had been thrillingly gutsy and diligent in their 1-0 win over City on Saturday and against PSG they were similarly solid at the back, but they lacked spark in attack. Ellie Carpenter became the focal point of their forward play from the right, with the striker Melvine Malard injured in the game against City.
PSG nullifying the threat of Carpenter blunted Chelsea, and despite their dominance of the ball, amassing 64% possession in the first half, Chelsea struggled to carve a way through the visitors’ backline. They had seven attempts on goal to PSG’s six at the break, despite 33 attacks to 10.
Chelsea have historically performed well against PSG, winning three of their four Champions League meetings prior to this penultimate fixture of their league phase campaign. In the 2018-19 quarter-finals they earned a 2-0 home win and, after a 2-1 away defeat, progressed to the semi-finals; in the 2022-23 season they won both group meetings with an overall score of 4-0.
The visiting team’s first attempt on target arrived after the break, with Merveille Kanjinga forcing a near-post save from Hannah Hampton. While Chelsea still dominated, PSG had more forays forward in the second half.
Erin Cuthbert, Maika Hamano and Lucy Bronze arrived at the hour mark as the home team sought to deal the killer blow their dominance required. It increasingly felt like it would take something special to break the deadlock, akin to the sublime effort that Sandy Baltimore had delivered against City.
Aggie Beever-Jones was replaced by Sjoeke Nüsken late on and the German instantly made a difference, forcing a sublime save from Katarzyna Kiedrzynek. The breakthrough came from the resulting corner, and it was far less sublime than Saturday’s effort, Buurman somehow squeezing the ball in at the near post after PSG failed to clear Cuthbert’s ball in.
“The main feeling is one of frustration,” said the PSG manager, Paulo César. “We defended well, we just lacked a bit of clarity on the transition and I have mixed feelings. I’m proud of my team but it shows that there are very fine margins that we need to rival a big team like Chelsea.”
Ultimately, the goal was the bit of luck Chelsea needed and they look increasingly formidable.

BK Häcken Women vs Manchester City Women. Women's Champions League.
Match report as Lauren Hemp and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw won the game for Man City at BK Hacken; the pair came on at half-time after a goalless first half; Mary Fowler saw a late penalty saved by Jennifer Falk; Man City remain unbeaten in the Women's Champions League this season
Lauren Hemp scored one and assisted another as Manchester City beat BK Hacken 2-0 in their penultimate Women's Champions League league phase game on Wednesday.
After a goalless first half in which the WSL champions struggled to break down a stubborn Hacken, Andree Jeglertz played his aces at half-time, bringing on Hemp and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw.
The England international immediately brought a spark and directness Man City had been lacking in the first 45 minutes. Aoba Fujino was their best attacking threat to that point, but was one of the players - along with Beth Mead, who was largely ineffective - who made way at the break.
It was a fortuitous opener for Hemp, although made by her own tenacity. She wriggled through two defenders into the box, with Emma Ostlund's clearance hitting her on the shin before beating Jennifer Falk.
She hit the post too not long after as Man City looked for the comfort of a second, and soon found it as Hemp and Shaw linked up perfectly.
It was almost telepathic as the winger picked up the ball deep on the left, lifting up her head for Shaw, who immediately began her run. The Jamaica international muscled through three defenders and once she had the ball at her feet, it was inevitable that she would beat the goalkeeper into the far corner.
There was late drama too as Man City were awarded a contentious penalty. Shaw went down after taking an elbow to the face from Aivi Luik as the two jumped for a high ball. The striker looked dazed as she went off the pitch, with the referee sent to the monitor by the VAR officials.
She eventually pointed to the spot with Mary Fowler stepping up. However, Falk guessed the right way as the Man City forward went for the bottom left corner.
But it did little to alter the overall result as Man City won their second Women's Champions League game, and it sends them into third on nine points. However, there are seven games yet to play on matchday five, with Jeglertz's side facing Austria Wien at home in their final league phase game on December 16.
38: BIG CHANCE! Fujino's shot is well-saved by Falk after a great run, before Yui Hasegawa skies the rebound.
45: CHANCE! Rebecca Knaack hits a wicked volley goalwards, but Falk is there to collect again.
52: SHOT!! Anna Anvegard's shot is blocked and cleared by Knaack.
55: GOAL! Hemp opens the scoring for Man City after a deflection off her shin.
57: NO GOAL! Fowler has the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up with Hasegawa standing in Falk's line of sight.
67: OFF THE POST! Hemp hits the woodwork after a great driving run, before Grace Clinton also sees her follow-up blocked.
77: GOAL! Shaw slots home after a fine pass from Hemp for Man City's second.
90+5: PENALTY! Man City are awarded a penalty after the referee was sent to the monitor by VAR. Luik is penalised for catching Shaw in the face with an elbow.
As if we needed a reminder, but it was clearer than ever just how influential Hemp and Shaw are for Man City after their half-time introduction.
Hemp was electric from the whistle. In the opening five minutes, she had already put in at least two crosses. Shaw made a key clearance at the other end too, proving that she can contribute across the pitch.
While Hemp's goal was created by talent and executed by luck, it was the second, as she pinged a ball forward for Shaw to finish, that truly showed why they are one of the most dangerous pairings in women's football. It was textbook from them both, but one that Hacken clearly had not studied.
Jeglertz would have been hoping to give his stars a rest, but they delivered when he needed them - ultimately what they are paid to do.
It was a shame Fujino had to be sacrificed. She was one of Man City's best players in the first half, but Beth Mead missed an opportunity to stake her claim for a regular starting spot. She offered little on her first Man City start since early October and will surely be disappointed.
But Hemp and Shaw reign supreme. It is a joy to watch them both play.
Man City boss Andree Jeglertz to the club's media: "A good game. We knew it would be a tough game to score against a very organised defending team. They have a great goalkeeper and we struggled in the first half. In the second half, they got a little bit tired, we got a little more space and we managed to get the goals.
"We try to get the best out of each player and put them in positions where they can really show what qualities they have.
"We have a great team together, we rotate players, and they all have a great impact on what we're doing. I think that will be very important in the future."

Club end deal early citing ‘differing commercial priorities’
Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt sponsor, BC Game, after the cryptocurrency casino’s partnership with a porn actor sparked a fan backlash. BC Game, an offshore company registered in Belize that is unlicensed to operate in the UK , had been Leicester’s main sponsor since 2024.
This month BC Game named Eva Elfie a brand ambassador, leading the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, to highlight the “devastating impacts” caused by gambling and pornography. On Wednesday the club said they prematurely ended their agreement with the online betting firm after they “recognised our differing commercial priorities”.
It is understood Leicester directly raised concerns with BC Game about the implications of their deal with Elfie, a Russian porn actor who BC Game said had “an established presence in gaming communities”. Leicester’s deal with BC Game, which began in July 2024, was due to run until the end of the season.
The trust had previously outlined concerns about the club’s partnership with BC Game. In a statement responding to the partnership this month, they said: “From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company we felt Leicester City were ditching its values.
“Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?”
Leicester, who visit Huddersfield in League One on Saturday, said supporters who purchased a shirt featuring BC Game branding within the past 28 days are able to exchange the shirt or are eligible for a full refund. The club added they would pay for the postage of returns via standard delivery.
Leicester remain for sale, with the club’s Thai owners, King Power, also seeking to sell their stadium, training base and women’s team.
In an unrelated development, the former Chelsea technical director Michael Emenalo is working as an adviser to the club, who are 11th in the third tier. Emenalo is among a team of Deloitte consultants Leicester say they have enlisted to “assess its current operations and inform its future strategic planning”.
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq4g:
BC Game has been the main shirt sponsor of Leicester City for two-and-a-half years
Leicester City have parted ways with their main shirt sponsor after the gambling firm appointed a porn actress as an ambassador.
BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the League One side at the start of the 2024-25 season - named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month .
The online gambling company posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin."
The club, which had faced criticism from fans' group The Foxes Trust, said it had reached a "mutual agreement" to end its partnership with the firm and fans who had bought shirts in the past 28 days could exchange them.
BC Game announced its new ambassador at the beginning of the month, prompting the trust to state: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.
"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"
On Wednesday the club issued a statement which said it and the sponsor had "reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect".
It also thanked the firm for the "constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement".
The statement confirmed an "enhanced returns policy" where it would accept BC Game branded shirts bought since 21 October for exchange or refund even if they had been worn or personalised.

Rockstar Games imzalı Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), oyun dünyasının en çok beklenen yapımları arasında yer alıyor. Jason ve Lucia karakterlerinin hikayesini konu alan oyun, Florida'dan ilham alınarak hazırlanan Leonida eyaletinde ve Vice City'de geçiyor. Yeni nesil konsollar için piyasaya sürülecek yapımın çıkış tarihi yaklaşırken Türkiye'deki oyuncular da GTA 6'nın ilk kez hangi gün ve saatte oynanabileceğini araştırıyor. Peki, GTA 6 Türkiye saatiyle saat kaçta çıkacak? İşte, GTA 6 PS5 / Xbox oynanış saati…
Rockstar Games'in açıkladığı takvime göre oyunun çıkış tarihi 19 Kasım 2026 Perşembe olarak belirlendi.
Türkiye'deki oyuncular, 18 Kasım Çarşamba gününü 19 Kasım Perşembe gününe bağlayan gece oyuna erişebilecek.
GTA 6 çıkış tarihi 2026 takviminde 19 Kasım olarak yer alırken konsol kullanıcıları da ilk oynanış için geri sayıma başladı.
GTA 6'nın Türkiye'de saat 00.00'da erişime açılması bekleniyor. Yerel saat dilimine göre uygulanacak çıkış takvimi doğrultusunda PlayStation 5 ve Xbox Series X|S kullanıcıları, 19 Kasım Perşembe günü gece yarısından itibaren oyunu oynayabilecek. GTA 6 Türkiye saatiyle 00.00'da mı çıkacak sorusunun yanıtı da böylece belli oluyor. Oyuncular, çıkış saatinden itibaren Vice City'nin açık dünyasına adım atabilecek.

Yönetmenliğini Ömer Faruk Sorak ve İpek Sorak'ın üstlendiği "Aşk Tesadüfleri Sever 3" filminin galası, İstanbul Paribu Cineverse Kanyon'da yapıldı.
Serinin üçüncü filminde, ilk iki yapımda olduğu gibi tesadüflerin bir araya getirdiği hayat hikayeleri beyaz perdeye taşınıyor. Galada filmin yönetmeni İpek Sorak ile oyuncular Mehmet Günsür ve Serkan Altunorak, AA muhabirine açıklamalarda bulundu.
Yönetmen Sorak, 16 yıllık süreçte "Aşk Tesadüfleri Sever" serisinin üç filme ulaştığını belirterek, "Bu, tesadüfleri anlatan bir seriye dönüştü. Biz de ister istemez gerçek hayattan alınmış tesadüf hikayelerini anlatırken bulduk kendimizi. Şu an çok heyecanlıyız. İzleyenler karar verecek ama ben çok mutluyum. Filmi izledikten sonra insanların salondan güzel bir duyguyla, umutla ayrılacağını düşünüyorum." ifadesini kullandı.
Çekimler sırasında kendisini duygulandıran pek çok an yaşadıklarını aktaran Sorak, bazı sahnelerde geçmişteki anları yeniden canlandırmanın kendileri için etkileyici bir deneyim olduğunu dile getirdi.
Sorak, filmin farklı yıllar arasında geçişler içermesi nedeniyle oyuncuların gençleştirilmesinde yapay zekadan yararlandıklarını belirterek, "Biz çok geçmişe gidip geliyoruz. 2012'ye, 2015'e, 2005'e, hatta 1960'lara gidiyoruz. Oyuncuları makyaj ve saçla o yaşlara götürmek biraz zor olabiliyor. Yeni teknikle çok güzel oldu. Yapay zekayla yaptığımız sahneler var ancak bunların hepsi hibrit. Birebir yapay zekayla bir şey üretmedik. Önce çekim yaptık, ardından bu görüntüler üzerinde yapay zekayla denemeler gerçekleştirdik." dedi.
Mehmet Günsür de aynı karakteri 16 yıl sonra yeniden canlandırmanın kendisi için özel bir deneyim olduğunu söyledi.
Günsür, "Aynı karakterle 16 sene sonra geri dönmek çok keyifliydi. O karakterin, Özgür'ün, 16 sene boyunca neler yaşayabileceğini düşünmek ve o şekilde hazırlanmak çok heyecan vericiydi. Her oyuncuya nasip olacak bir şey değil, 16 sene önceki karakterin 16 sene sonraki halini gösterme şansını bulmak." diye konuştu.
Bazı sahneleri yeniden canlandırmanın kendisinde zaman yolculuğu hissi uyandırdığını aktaran Günsür, "Kendimi zaman yolculuğu yapmış gibi hissettiğim anlar oldu. Sanki 16 sene öncesine gittim. Çünkü bazı aynı sahneleri yeniden canlandırdık." sözlerini sarf etti.
Günsür canlandırdığı karakterin gelişimiyle ilgili olarak ise "16 sene boyunca hep direnmiş bir bariyeri yıkmaya, hep direnmiş ama 16 sene sonra karşısına birtakım olaylar zinciri ve bir kadın çıkıyor ve 16 yıl boyunca direndiği noktayı kırmak için cesaret alıyor diyeyim. Keyifliydi." bilgisini paylaştı.
Yapay zekanın filmdeki kullanımını da beğendiğini dile getiren oyuncu, "Hibrit olarak kullanıldı. Yüzde yüz yapay zeka değil, bizim çektiğimiz görüntülere uygulandı. Bence çok iyi çalışıyor." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Filmde Emre karakterini canlandıran Serkan Altunorak ise devam filminde rol almanın kendisi için farklı bir tecrübe olduğunu ifade etti.
Altunorak, canlandırdığı karakterin hikayesine ilişkin, "Emre'yi oynuyorum. Devrim Özkan'ın oynadığı Mavi karakteriyle üniversiteden beri beraber olan, reklamcılık dünyasında iddialı bir ajansa sahip iki kişinin arasındaki ilişkiyi izliyoruz. Mehmet Günsür'ün oynadığı Özgür karakterinin bir kampanya vesilesiyle hayatlarına girmesiyle olaylar değişiyor." dedi.
Reklamcılık sektörünün filmde işlenen yönlerine de değinen Altunorak, "Reklam dünyası çok acımasız bir dünya. Her ne kadar savunmadığım tarafları olsa da artık sistemin bununla döndüğü gerçeğiyle yaşadığımız bir dünyadayız. Bazı anları oynamakta, bazı cümleleri söylemekte bile zorlandım. Çünkü beynim asla kabul etmiyordu." ifadesini kullandı.
Filmin kendi kariyerinde de farklı bir deneyim olduğunu belirten Altunorak, "Daha önce hiçbir devam filminde oynamamıştım. Kendi içinde kült olmuş, seyirciyle çok doğrudan bağ kurmuş bir filmin devamında yer almak ve bu başarının içinde olmak beni mutlu etti." diye konuştu.
Mehmet Günsür ile daha önce "Muhteşem Yüzyıl" dizisinde de birlikte rol aldıklarını hatırlatan Altunorak, "Çok yakın bir dostluğumuz var. Daha önce 'Muhteşem Yüzyıl'da da beraber oynamıştık. Orada da partnerdik ve müthiş bir set geçirmiştik. Neredeyse 12-13 yıl sonra kaldığımız yerden devam ettik. Bütün oyuncularla birlikte çok keyifli, her anlamda eğlenceli ve güzel bir set tecrübesiydi." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Galada organ bağışına yönelik farkındalık çalışması da gerçekleştirildi. Sağlık Bakanlığı tarafından etkinlik alanında kurulan stantta katılımcılara organ bağışı hakkında bilgilendirme yapıldı. Galaya katılan piyanist Ece Dağıstan da organ bağışı konusundaki kişisel deneyimini ve farkındalık çalışmalarını paylaştı.
Dağıstan, filmde organ bağışı üzerine işlenen anlatının toplumsal farkındalık oluşturabileceğini belirtti. Yaklaşık 8 yıldır organ bağışı kampanyaları düzenlediğini aktaran Dağıstan, ablasının uzun süre böbrek yetmezliği yaşaması üzerine ona böbreğini bağışladığını anlattı.
Bu deneyimin kendisinde organ bağışına yönelik daha güçlü bir duyarlılık oluşturduğunu ifade eden Dağıstan, "Daha çok insana ulaşmak, bu konuyu daha basite indirgemek istiyorum. Organ bekleyen binlerce insan var ancak maalesef ülkemizde bu konu biraz yavaş tempoda ilerliyor. Bu filmin birçok insanda farklı duygular uyandıracağına eminim. Bu konuda bir yaptırım değil, insanları teşvik etme niyetiyle anlatıyorum. Bu film bence çok iyi bir duyarlılık yaratacak, farkındalık yaratacak bu konuyla ilgili o yüzden çok müteşekkirim." diye konuştu.

İki Oscar ödüllü Hollywood oyuncusu Hilary Swank, 52 yaşında üçüncü çocuğunu beklemesine yönelik eleştirilere cevap verdi. Katıldığı bir televizyon programında konuşan Swank, ileri yaşta anne olmanın artık olağan bir durum olduğunu savundu.
Habertürk'ün aktardığına göre Swank, programda şu ifadeleri kullandı: "Çağa ayak uydurmanın zamanı geldi! Dünyamız çok ilerledi, insanlar çok daha uzun yaşıyor ve birçok kadın daha geç yaşta çocuk sahibi olmak istiyor, bu da oldukça normal bir durum haline geliyor."
Oyuncu, iki hamileliğini de karşılaştırdı. Tek bebek taşımanın ikizlere göre çok daha kolay olduğunu söyleyen Swank, ikizlerine hamileyken üçüncü trimesterin üçüncü haftasına kadar çalıştığını, günde 18 saat sette kaldığını ve iki dublörle çalıştığını anlattı. Dublörlerin fazla mesai yapamadığını hatırlatan Swank, "Ama hamile, yaşlı kadın yapabiliyordu" dedi.
Swank, üçüncü çocuğunu beklediğini ekim ayında sosyal medya hesabından duyurmuştu. Oyuncu o paylaşımda "Birçok kişi bir sonraki projemin ne olduğunu soruyor, bu proje aralık ayında yayınlanacak" ifadesini kullanmıştı.
Ünlü oyuncu, eşi Philip Schneider ile birlikte 2023 yılında, 48 yaşındayken ikiz bebek sahibi olmuştu. Swank'ın 37 yaşında yumurtalarını dondurduğu biliniyor.
Swank, "Boys Don't Cry" ve "Million Dollar Baby" filmlerindeki rolleriyle En İyi Kadın Oyuncu dalında iki kez Oscar kazandı. Anne olmadan önce kariyerine odaklanabildiği için kendini şanslı saydığını belirten oyuncu, "Kariyerim dikkatimi vermek istediğim bebeğim gibiydi, dikkatimi dağıtacak şeyler istemiyordum" dedi.
Bugünkü hayatından da memnun olduğunu söyleyen Swank, "İki çocuğum var, harika bir kocam var, harika bir ailem var, destek görüyorum. Gerçekten çok şanslıyım ve daha mutlu olamazdım" diye konuştu.

It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again
I n many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.
Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.
In the six years after being crowned kings of Europe, United turned to Wilf McGuinness, Busby stepped in temporarily to keep them up, then Frank O’Farrell was appointed before they landed on Tommy Docherty, who experienced the ignominy of taking them down.
In the past eight years, United have sacked José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjær, Erik ten Hag , Ruben Amorim and now Michael Carrick .
How did the United of 1974 go down? Most outsiders believed they were too big to fail. Inside the club, though, they sensed the direction of travel. After a heavy defeat at Crystal Palace in December 1972, Busby offered Docherty the job in the Selhurst Park boardroom. “There’s a lot of trouble in the camp,” Busby said. Docherty was doing well as Scotland manager and took a few days to mull it over, but decided he couldn’t turn down the opportunity.
When Busby called him on the Sunday evening, he accepted. “You know it won’t be easy?” Busby said. “It’ll be like turning an oil tanker round, only bigger.” He added: “You might find yourself having to take a step back in order to take a leap forward.” Docherty wrote in his autobiography, The Doc, that at the time he never believed Busby was alluding to relegation.
Docherty was given free rein for a rebuild. The day after his appointment, he signed George Graham from Arsenal for £120,000, a sizeable fee at the time. Alex Forsyth followed from Partick for £100,000 and Docherty pulled off a coup when he persuaded Lou Macari to join bottom-of-the-table United instead of Liverpool for £200,000.
The giants of the previous era were moved on. In February, Bobby Charlton told him that, at 37, it would be his last season. Other big names wanted to stay, but Docherty felt a reset was needed. “The Manchester United team that had won the European Cup in 1968 was without a doubt a great team, but many members of that side had been allowed to grow old together,” he wrote.
“I knew what I had decided would prove very unpopular with many people but it had to be done. I set out my stall to end the United careers of among others Denis Law, Tony Dunne, Pat Crerand and David Sadler.”
George Best, who had retired once but returned under Docherty, played his last game on New Year’s Day 1974 after repeatedly turning up late. The most controversial departure was Law, who was allowed to join Manchester City.
Having taken over with United bottom, Docherty kept them up in his first season and was emboldened to continue his clearout. Thirteen players were released that summer. But halfway through the following season they were facing relegation again and a lack of goals cost them. At one stage, the joint-top scorer was Alex Stepney, with two penalties. He was the goalkeeper.
Relegation was confirmed on the penultimate day as they lost to City, a defeat made all the more painful by Law back-heeling the late winner. Docherty was interviewed on the Old Trafford pitch and asked, in a scene replayed in TNT Sports’ Too Good To Go Down, whether the club would drift into obscurity. “No, there’s no danger,” he said. “We could wash the jerseys here and hang them out to dry and you’d get 15,000 people standing watching them do so.”
Despite the bravado, Docherty was expecting the sack when he met Busby a few days later. Instead, Busby handed him a case of champagne, reminded him of the oil tanker and told him to set to work getting them back up.
Docherty’s prediction proved right: the brand was far bigger than the division they played in. In the Second Division, Old Trafford averaged crowds of more than 47,000 – the biggest in the country – and their away support descended on towns and cities and routinely outnumbered the home contingent.
Docherty bought young and hungry, targeting players with a point to prove, including Steve Coppell from Tranmere, Stuart Pearson from Hull and Jim Holton from Shrewsbury. The direct, attacking football synonymous with United returned and the Scot shaped a fearless 4-2-4 formation.
Crowds grew after they came straight back up and for a while United were on course to become the fifth side to win the First Division after promotion, but finished third and also reached the FA Cup final, losing 1-0 to Southampton. That shows the stark differences between then and now.
The gap between the first and second tiers was narrower. United did not lose a gargantuan broadcast deal when they went down. They were not saddled with debt by their owners. Their wage bill was not tied to Champions League qualification. Players were not on long contracts and were easier to buy and sell. There were no disruptive agents. Fans were more patient.
If lessons of the 1970s are not heeded soon, the fallout could be infinitely more painful.

Jess Carter made 83 appearances across all competitions for Gotham FC
England defender Jess Carter has completed a move to Bay FC after leaving Gotham FC as a free agent.
The 29-year-old has signed a contract that will keep her with Bay FC - a club based in the San Francisco Bay Area - until 2028, with the option for an additional year.
Carter joined New York-side Gotham in July 2024 after a six-year spell with Chelsea that saw her win the Women's Super League on five occasions.
"Coming to Bay FC is a new challenge, and that's something I'm excited about," said Carter.
"I've been fortunate to be part of some successful teams, and I know how much work goes into winning. I'm looking forward to getting to know this group, earning the trust of my team-mates and doing my part to help us move forward."
Carter played in all 30 of Gotham's matches in 2026 as the club won the NWSL Shield - given to the league's regular-season champions.
She also helped Gotham win the NWSL Championship in 2025, when they defeated Washington Spirit in the final.
"Jess has been a big part of what we've accomplished as a club, and we're very thankful for the contributions she's made during her time here," said Yael Averbuch West, the president of football operations for Gotham.
Carter, who has 56 senior England caps, was part of the squad that won the 2022 European Championships, while she appeared in all six games as the Lionesses defended their title last summer.
"Jess has consistently demonstrated her quality in championship-winning environments at both club and international level," said Bay FC's chief football officer Paul Green, who worked with Carter at Chelsea.
"I've seen her development and the professionalism she brings every day. She will bring valuable experience to Bay FC, and we're delighted to welcome her to the club."

Mudryk joined Chelsea in a deal worth up to £89m in January 2023
On-loan Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk says he blames the administration of the Ukraine national team for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban from football.
The 25-year-old, on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, which he believes entered his system while on international duty.
Having initially faced a four-year ban from the Football Association (FA), his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport was successful.
He returned to football after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules and agreeing to a suspension equivalent to the time he had already served.
After appearing for Chelsea during a pre-season tour of Asia, Mudryk joined Tottenham on transfer deadline day to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto de Zerbi.
In a lengthy interview with the Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk was asked who he blamed for his absence from the game.
"The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team," he replied. "It should never have existed. I probably haven't said it publicly yet, but I'm saying it now.
"I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England."
He explained how he had only been in Ukraine to be with the national team and "it points to the fact it was in a national team camp".
Asked specifically whether he blamed the national team, Mudryk replied: "Yes, exactly."
He also said Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko offered little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and claimed its handling of the matter delayed his return to football.
Mudryk also said he spent millions of pounds on legal fees, coaching, pitch hire and private physiotherapy while being unable to access services at Chelsea .
He added: "It was a bolt from the blue. I couldn't believe it [the positive test] was true.
"It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on falling. It hit me very hard, mentally."
Mudryk said he cried and drank alcohol after the initial suspension but never doubted that he would eventually return to top-level football.
Last year a UAF spokesperson told BBC Sport it was "in close contact with Mudryk's lawyers" but had not been contacted by the FA about the case.

Strasbourg have announced the appointment of Swansea City 's Vitor Matos as the club's new head coach.
The French top-flight side made the announcement on Wednesday evening, but there has been no official confirmation of Matos' departure from the Swans.
Strasbourg are expected to pay Swansea compensation thought to be in the region of £5m in order to secure his services.
Matos, 38, spent just under a year at Swansea having left his role at Maritimo to succeed Alan Sheehan as the Championship club's head coach in November 2025.
Four members of Matos' coaching team - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira - are also expected to leave Swansea.
Ex-captain Ashley Williams is set to return to the club to join an interim coaching team also featuring fellow former players Kristian O'Leary and Leon Britton.
O'Leary and Britton are set to be the only remaining members of Matos' Swansea staff.
Alongside Williams, they will lead Swansea while the club searches for Matos' permanent successor.
Their first game will be at home to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.
Swansea go to Middlesbrough next Tuesday before hosting rivals Cardiff City on Sunday, 29 November.
Matos moves on despite agreeing an extended Swansea contract running until 2030 in July.
Leon Britton (left) and Ashley Williams (right) were Swansea team-mates in League One, the Championship and the Premier League
Swansea were 20th in the second tier when the former Liverpool coach took over, but he leaves a team lying only three points off the top of the table in sixth.
Matos led Swansea to an 11th-placed finish last season, and has raised hopes of a potential promotion push in 2026-27 thanks to an encouraging start to this campaign.
But he told Swansea he wanted to move on after Strasbourg, who have the same ownership group as Premier League side Chelsea, made their move last weekend and he said goodbye to players and staff on Tuesday.
Having finished eighth last season, Strasbourg are 13th in Ligue 1 having won only three of their 10 league games under Hugo Oliveira, who was only appointed in the summer after Gary O'Neil departed to take over at Ipswich Town.
Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds
Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he had also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea.
When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better."
In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs.
But Gorringe played down the idea of Matos being lured away, saying: "The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch.
"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.
"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time."

The Football Association has considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, BBC Sport can reveal.
But it believes any attempt to prevent him from standing in the election in March is likely to fail.
The FA has also confirmed it is backing rival candidate Philippe Diallo.
Infantino oversaw the introduction of a three-term limit when he replaced Sepp Blatter as leader of world football's governing body.
However, Fifa's council agreed in 2022 that his first period in office from 2016 to 2019 should not count as it was the remainder of his predecessor's interrupted final term after resigning.
Earlier this month, human rights campaign group Fair Square wrote to the FA claiming that the decision is open to legal challenge and was "contrary to the spirit and purpose" of Fifa statutes.
It urged the FA to ask Fifa's governance committee to bar Infantino from the election in March because he has already served the maximum three terms.
FA chair Debbie Hewitt has now replied, telling Fair Square that the governing body "has explored the possibility of challenging Mr Infantino's eligibility to run for a further term as the Fifa president but does not consider that such a challenge would secure the outcome sought".
In correspondence seen by the BBC, Hewitt adds: "Ultimately the process followed Fifa's governance and led to an outcome where Mr Infantino's part term was disregarded for the purposes of maximum term limits.
"Having considered the process in detail, we do not believe that a challenge would succeed."
In a statement, Fair Square said: "It's understandable that the FA has no faith in Fifa's internal processes to hold Infantino accountable for serious breaches of the rules, but it's a mistake to abandon these channels, not least because it sends a signal to Infantino that he can do whatever he likes.
"We will encourage the FA to leave its options open where this matter is concerned not least because Debbie Hewitt's position on the Fifa council puts her in a very strong position to demand clear answers on why Fifa discounted Infantino's first term."
Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - has said a national association or confederation may need to challenge Infantino's eligibility at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas).
However he has also said that the ability of European football associations to do so has been made harder by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin deciding to stand for a fourth term earlier this year. Ceferin reversed a previous insistence, in 2024, he would not seek re-election.
The FA was among a number of national associations to withdraw its support of Infantino in the wake of the crisis sparked by his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.
European confederation Uefa has backed rival candidate Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation.
Hewitt, who became a member of Fifa's council in 2023, also told Fair Square that the FA "remains opposed to Mr Infantino's re-election and is committed to providing its full support to Philippe Diallo as our preferred candidate in the upcoming Fifa presidential election".
Last month Hewitt told BBC Sport that Infantino was not fit to lead world football unless he released documents and answered questions relating to the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan.
It has previously referred to the fact that in 2022 its council "unanimously confirmed its agreement with the view of the governance, audit & compliance committee that the period between 2016 and 2019 does not count as a term of office for the current Fifa president, who is therefore about to end his first term".

Real Madrid, milli futbolcu Arda Güler'in sözleşmesini 2032 yılına kadar uzattığını duyurdu.
Kulübün resmi sitesinden yapılan açıklamada, "Real Madrid ve Arda Güler, oyuncumuzun sözleşmesini 30 Haziran 2032 tarihine kadar uzatmak üzere anlaşmaya vardı" denildi.
Açıklamada Arda Güler'in Real Madrid'e Temmuz 2023'te 18 yaşındayken katıldığı ve dört sezon boyunca 126 maça çıktığı belirtildi.
Ayrıca Güler'in Real Madrid formasıyla 1 Şampiyonlar Ligi, 1 FIFA Kulüpler Dünya Kupası, 1 UEFA Süper Kupa, 1 La Liga şampiyonluğu ve 1 İspanya Süper Kupası kazandığı kaydedildi.
38 kez Türkiye A Milli Takımı'nın formasını giyen Arda Güler'in ayrıca Eylül ayında 2025-2026 Şampiyonlar Ligi'nin "Çıkış Yapan Oyuncusu" ödülüne layık görüldüğü vurgulandı.
Kulübün resmi X hesabından yapılan paylaşımda da "Tarih yazılacak" denildi ve Arda Güler'in görüntüleri yer aldı.
Gençlerbirliği altyapısında futbola başlayan Arda Güler, 16 yaşında iken ilk kez Fenerbahçe A Takımı'nda forma giydi.
19 Ağustos 2021'de UEFA Avrupa Ligi eleme maçında Fenerbahçe'nin HJK Helsinki'yi 1-0 yendiği karşılaşmada 66. dakikada oyuna girdi.
Arda Güler, 13 Mart 2022'de Fenerbahçe'nin Alanyaspor'u 5-2 yendiği maçta attığı golle, kulübün tarihinde lig maçlarındaki en genç golcüsü olmuştu.
Aynı maçta bir de asist yapan Arda Güler, o dönem 17 yaşındaydı.
Arda Güler, 19 Kasım 2022'de Çek Cumhuriyeti'ne karşı oynanan maçta ilk kez milli takım forması giymiş, dördüncü milli maçında Galler karşısında fileleri havalandırmıştı.

Mauricio Pochettino said it was “an honour” and “a privilege” to be the new Manchester United head coach after arriving in England on Wednesday.
Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight after overseeing the USA beating Haiti in his final game in charge. Members of Pochettino’s staff landed earlier in the week to begin work at Carrington , laying the foundations as United seek to turn their season around. His right-hand man, Jesús Pérez, the goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and the fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino, who continues to work with his father, have already taken training with those not on international duty.
Those away with their national teams will return to the club on Thursday, when they are expected to meet Pochettino for the first time and hold meetings. Conversations have also been held with various departments within the club, as Pochettino sought to learn about the squad’s health as he seeks areas of improvement.
Pochettino’s first challenge will be at Anfield on Sunday, when 18th-placed United take on Liverpool. The 54-year-old has his eyes set on rattling Manchester City after being told on TNT Sports that “Manchester’s blue and always will be blue” by DaMarcus Beasley, who once had a loan spell with City. Pochettino responded: “No way. You will see. Give me time … give me time and that is going to start to change.”
Speaking about joining United, Pochettino said: “It’s a big challenge but at the same time, it’s adrenaline that you want to feel because I think we are going to have a different job. But I think one of the things that is important is that we have the experience to deal with that, and I think we need to add our common sense and the way we are going to approach all the things.
“We know that the situation is not a situation that a club like Manchester United deserves,” Pochettino added. “The fanbase is amazing and after we signed here in America, of every 10 people I crossed in the street, nine are Manchester United fans. It’s amazing.”
Pochettino is also reunited with the strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya, the analyst Alec Scott and his long-term assistant, Miki D’Agostino, at Old Trafford.

With his team mired in the relegation zone and a massive match at Liverpool this weekend, Mauricio Pochettino has been understandably busy since being appointed head coach of Manchester United. Unfortunately for Old Trafford regulars, the small print of his contract meant the Argentinian was tied up masterminding victory for USA USA USA in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti when he ought to have been in Carrington moving red magnets around a tactics board in front of Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire.
The match in Cincinnati was ostensibly a dead rubber, given the hosts kicked off with a 6-0 lead. However, the conditions of Pochettino’s release clause dictated he had to remain in charge until finishing his post-match media duties at the TQL Stadium. Like an errant spouse having one last dinner with their put-upon partner while their lover waits outside the restaurant with the engine running, Pochettino was unable to make his excuses and leave until the bill was settled. It was no surprise that his new role came up during his exit interview. In a playful exchange with DaMarcus Beasley, who spent a season on loan at Manchester City during the (Ben) Thatcher era, something of a gauntlet was thrown down to the departing boss. “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue,” honked the former international, who may be unaware of his former club’s disgrace and potentially imminent relegation to the North West Counties League.
“No way, you will see,” chuckled Pochettino by way of response. “Give me time. Give me time and that is going to change, for sure.” While the future colour scheme of football in Manchester almost certainly lies more in the hands of the three-person independent panel who will decide City’s fate after finding them guilty of industrial scale financial shenanigans, Pochettino assured fans he and his staff will do their bit to ensure the city will be painted red. “We are excited because the new challenge is a big challenge,” he whooped. “But at the same time, it’s the adrenaline that you want to feel. We are going to have a different job, but we have the experience to deal with that. We know that it is not a situation that deserves to be at a club like Manchester United and for the fanbase. The fanbase is amazing.”
Considering they’ve been flirting with Pochettino for nine years, most United fans will be unconcerned by his eventual arrival being delayed by an extra couple of days but, with that game against Liverpool to prepare for, the 54-year-old wasted little time in hightailing it to the airport and boarding a private jet for his new home. Upon arrival, he is expected to oversee his first training session, an event Sky Sports News has melodramatically anticipated using a serene, high-budget cinematic aesthetic that captures our Argentinian hero gazing longingly into a Manchester sunset. It’s a majestic, blockbuster shot that has rightfully become the subject of no end of online mockery. Football Daily wonders if we’ll see a contrasting shot on Sunday, when the Sky cameras cut to Pochettino staring in wide-eyed horror as Liverpool spank yet another goal past his side’s hapless defence.
